status: Result trust rotation and command wiring verified locally; chart installation and end-to-end delivery remain incomplete

environment.API: Fake Kubernetes clients; real local mTLS listeners for endpoint and delivery tests

proved: The result rotator persists candidate private material and two independent retirement timestamps. Each timestamp follows direct enrollment-policy readback; delayed writes do not shorten the maximum-credential-lifetime plus five-minute-skew wait. Restart and uncertain write responses retain the same candidate and bounds.

Policy publication precedes projection changes. A rolled-back policy after a wait starts, missing installation objects, foreign metadata, replacement projection/policy UIDs, and malformed journals are refused. Bootstrap uses only precreated objects; no Secret CREATE permission is required.

The rotation first expands both trust bundles, then switches the server leaf and client signer, then retires old roots and private material after both waits and endpoint checks. A leaf that would expire during the first wait is renewed under the old CA first. Tests cover leaf renewal and expired stable authorities with a fake clock and fake endpoint probe.

Real mTLS probes check every ready endpoint against an unchanged EndpointSlice identity snapshot, the exact server leaf, and every still-valid overlap client CA. HEAD without an operation identity must return HTTP 401. Missing client trust, a different leaf, absent ready endpoints, or changed endpoint identity fails.

The command requires all five result object flags together and dedicated Secrets, Service, and Lease. Independent result and webhook supervisors start concurrently, enforce separate operation deadlines, aggregate readiness, and both stop when the service stops. Persisting a transition without an endpoint verdict does not claim readiness.
